blocks.heading: Reuse is a tool
blocks.body:
A pointer that saves twenty identical warnings is useful. A pointer that saves one sentence is extra work. A pointer that shares a half-wrong warning is a defect.

Reuse **small**, **stable**, **true in every place it appears**. Copy when the sentence will drift, or appears once, or is product-specific safety text.

Never edit the pulled copy on the how-to. Change the source, or write a local note.

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
You just met the idea. Now do the lab: Retire one weak reuse.

This lab can fail. Fail when: You retired nothing, or you deleted a still-shared warning without replacing it, or the rule file is slogans with no example.

Expected: One fewer library id, or one converted local note. A three-bullet rule file. Pack still clean.

blocks.lead: Walk the cards below, in order, to Retire one weak reuse.
blocks.intro: How to Retire one weak reuse. Walk the cards in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Retire one weak reuse
steps.body: This is the whole move. The next cards are the steps, in order.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: Look at the three library notes. Pick the weakest: too specific, too vague, or used only once with no second home.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Replace that pointer with a local note on the how-to. Delete the library id if nothing else uses it.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Write oxygen-bootcamp-work/week4/reuse-worse.txt with three bullets: (1) what you retired, (2) why a local sentence won, (3) what you still reuse.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Do not retire pinch-hazard if it is still used twice and still true. Pick a real weak one, or add a bad reuse (a whole marketing paragraph) and then retire that.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: Completeness clean. The how-to still opens with no red error.

blocks.q: A sentence is reused on one page and will not appear anywhere else. Keep the pointer?
options: Yes :  a pointer is always cleaner
No :  you paid for a pointer that helps no one
Yes if the id looks stable
blocks.why: Single-use reuse is extra machinery. A local sentence is cheaper.

blocks.lead: Answer with words from today only.
blocks.q: Two products need opposite warnings. One library note tries to cover both with vague wording. What do you do?
options: Write two notes, or two local notes :  do not share a sentence that is half wrong
Hide the note by changing Author colors
blocks.why: A shared sentence that is half wrong is a defect. Reuse is not a prize.
